blocks.title: Alkanes
blocks.text: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2. Methane, CH4, is the simplest member of the family.

What is obtained after removing one hydrogen atom from an alkane is an alkyl group, named by replacing the -ane of the alkane with -yl: methane gives methyl, CH3- (Me-), and ethane gives ethyl, CH3CH2- (Et-) (Table 11.2). For alkanes with more than two carbon atoms, more than one alkyl group can be derived (Table 11.3): from propane, n-propyl (propyl) CH3CH2CH2- and isopropyl (1-methylethyl) CH3CH(CH3)-; from butane, n-butyl (butyl), sec-butyl (1-methylpropyl), isobutyl (2-methylpropyl) and tert-butyl (1,1-dimethylethyl; printed '1,1-dimethylpropyl'). Butane is the fuel in lighters and isobutane a propellant in shaving gel.

blocks.prompt: Eicosane is a straight-chain alkane with 20 carbon atoms. Give its molecular formula, and write the structural formulas of 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane (Quick Check 11.1a, d).
blocks.explanation: CnH2n+2 with n = 20 gives C20H42. 2-Methylbutane: CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3, a four-carbon chain with a methyl on carbon 2. 2,2-Dimethylpropane: C(CH3)4, a three-carbon chain with two methyls on carbon 2; both are C5H12.

items: Alkanes CnH2n+2, saturated, methane to decane (Table 11.1); each member differs by CH2.
Alkyl group = alkane minus one H, -ane to -yl: methyl, ethyl, n- and isopropyl, n-, sec-, iso- and tert-butyl.
